display.title: Elul: Chasing Away the Yetzer Hara with Good Thoughts
display.summary_short: In Elul the King is close and even hears our thoughts. Uncle Yossi teaches children to chase away the yetzer hara by replacing bad thoughts with holy ones.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show in the first week of Elul. Uncle Yossi explains that Elul is the month of mercy, when Hashem is like a King in the field who receives everyone with a shining face, as the Alter Rebbe teaches. To become better, we start with our thoughts. The yetzer hara is tricky: first he sends a bad thought, then gets us to talk about it, then to do it. Since Hashem hears our thoughts as clearly as spoken words, we must keep only good thoughts. The yetzer hara is also a coward who runs when we yell at him. The best weapon is to think of something holy right away: the words of the Shema, Shivisi Hashem, picturing the four letters of Hashem's name (which we say with a 'K' out of respect), and the Twelve Pesukim, which every soldier in Tzivos Hashem should say daily and think about often.
display.lesson: Hashem hears our thoughts, so when a bad thought comes, replace it right away with a holy one.
